**Abbott Laboratories (CIK 1800), fiscal year ended 31 December 2024**

**Headline profitability**

| Metric (USD, FY) | 2024 | 2023 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Net sales | $41.950B | $40.109B | +4.6% |
| Operating income | $6.825B | $6.478B | +5.4% |
| Pretax income | $7.013B | $6.664B | +5.2% |
| Income tax (benefit) expense | $(6.389)B | $0.941B | — |
| Net income | $13.402B | $5.723B | +134% |
| Diluted EPS | $7.64 | $3.26 | +134% |

Source: FY2024 Form 10-K, accession 0001628280-25-007110 (filed 2025-02-21), fact IDs 1550474, 1545490, 1539913, 1540997, 1544911, 1537651; prior-year comparatives 1550465, 1545481, 1539904, 1540988, 1544902, 1537642.

**What changed**

Net margin rose from 14.3% to 31.9% (calculated: 5,723/40,109 vs 13,402/41,950), a gain of about 17.7 percentage points. Operating margin, however, was essentially flat — 16.2% in 2023 versus 16.3% in 2024 (calculated), a change of only about 0.1 pp. So the reported profitability surge was almost entirely below the operating line.

**Main driver: a one-off, non-cash tax benefit**

The 10-K states that fourth-quarter 2024 taxes on earnings include "$7.5 billion in non-cash valuation allowance adjustments resulting from the restructuring of certain foreign affiliates and the confirmation of certain tax filing positions," because management concluded the previously fully reserved deferred tax assets were more likely than not realizable (Note 15, Taxes on Earnings; chunk 1800/abt-20241231:267200). The tax note table confirms this: total deferred tax was $(7,961) million in 2024 versus $(461) million in 2023, with foreign deferred tax of $(7,502) million versus $(79) million (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:273600). The effective-rate reconciliation shows a (107.1) pp "valuation allowance adjustments" line in 2024 versus nil in 2023. Absent this item, pretax income rose only 5.2% and the effective tax rate would have been roughly in line with 2023's ~14%.

**Operating drivers (modest, and mixed)**

- Medical Devices: operating earnings +16.0%; segment operating margin 31.4% → 32.4%, on broad sales growth including CGM ($6.4B vs $5.3B) (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:92800, 94400).
- Nutrition: operating earnings +12.9%; margin 16.4% → 17.9% on higher sales, pricing and margin initiatives (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:96000).
- Established Pharmaceuticals: operating earnings +2.2%; margin 23.7% in 2024 (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:97600).
- Diagnostics: operating earnings −14.8%, margin down to 22.2%, driven by continued lower COVID-19 test demand (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:94400).
- Other (income) expense, net fell to $376M from $479M, partly reflecting a $143M loss on sale of a non-core Established Pharmaceutical business (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:131200).

**Interpretation caveat:** the 2024 net-income and EPS increase is largely an accounting/tax event, not an improvement in underlying operating profitability. Operating margin was essentially unchanged year over year.

**What changed**

Net margin rose from 14.3% to 31.9% (calculated: 5,723/40,109 vs 13,402/41,950), a gain of about 17.7 percentage points. Operating margin, however, was essentially flat — 16.2% in 2023 versus 16.3% in 2024 (calculated), a change of only about 0.1 pp. So the reported profitability surge was almost entirely below the operating line.

**Main driver: a one-off, non-cash tax benefit**

The 10-K states that fourth-quarter 2024 taxes on earnings include "$7.5 billion in non-cash valuation allowance adjustments resulting from the restructuring of certain foreign affiliates and the confirmation of certain tax filing positions," because management concluded the previously fully reserved deferred tax assets were more likely than not realizable (Note 15, Taxes on Earnings; chunk 1800/abt-20241231:267200). The tax note table confirms this: total deferred tax was $(7,961) million in 2024 versus $(461) million in 2023, with foreign deferred tax of $(7,502) million versus $(79) million (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:273600). The effective-rate reconciliation shows a (107.1) pp "valuation allowance adjustments" line in 2024 versus nil in 2023. Absent this item, pretax income rose only 5.2% and the effective tax rate would have been roughly in line with 2023's ~14%.

**Operating drivers (modest, and mixed)**

- Medical Devices: operating earnings +16.0%; segment operating margin 31.4% → 32.4%, on broad sales growth including CGM ($6.4B vs $5.3B) (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:92800, 94400).
- Nutrition: operating earnings +12.9%; margin 16.4% → 17.9% on higher sales, pricing and margin initiatives (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:96000).
- Established Pharmaceuticals: operating earnings +2.2%; margin 23.7% in 2024 (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:97600).
- Diagnostics: operating earnings −14.8%, margin down to 22.2%, driven by continued lower COVID-19 test demand (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:94400).
- Other (income) expense, net fell to $376M from $479M, partly reflecting a $143M loss on sale of a non-core Established Pharmaceutical business (chunk 1800/abt-20241231:131200).

**Interpretation caveat:** the 2024 net-income and EPS increase is largely an accounting/tax event, not an improvement in underlying operating profitability. Operating margin was essentially unchanged year over year.
